sentences.text: Aggrieved by the compensation fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondent/claimant sought reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, and the Reference Court initially passed an order dated 25.11.1992.
However, pursuant to an order of remand by the High Court, the learned Reference Court, taken up the matter for fresh consideration.
Before the learned Reference Court, on behalf of the State, the Referring Officer was examined as PW1 and Exs.A1 to A7 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent/claimant RWs1 to 5 were examined and Exs.X1 to X3 were marked.

4. The learned Reference Court after considering the matter with reference to the oral and documentary evidences, fixed the market value of the acquired site @ Rs.2,000/- per cent as against Rs.3,000/- per cent claimed by the respondent.
Feeling aggrieved by the said fixation, the State preferred the present appeal.
5. Mr. T S Rayulu, learned Government Pleader, made submissions inter alia to the effect that the learned Reference Court erred in relying on Ex.X1, Sale transaction of the year, 1960.

He submits that the learned Reference Court erred in arriving its conclusions with reference to Exs.X1 and X2 without conducting any independent enquiry, that the enhancement is highly excessive, without any valid basis and the order under challenge is not sustainable.
6. We have considered the submissions made and on perusal of the material on record, we are not inclined to accept the contentions advanced by the learned Government Pleader.

As per the evidence adduced on behalf of the respondent/claimant, Chabolu Village wherein the subject matter land is situate is adjacent to the Gananpuram Village and the distance between the said villages is about 2 Kms.
Ex.X1 is a Registered Sale deed dated 23.07.1960 in respect of the land situate in Gananpuram village and the sale consideration was Rs.3,000/- for 3 cents.

More than 15 years after the said Contd...
NJS,J & TMR,J sale transaction, the subject matter lands were acquired and it is also not in dispute that they are in the centre of the village.

7. That apart, the learned Reference Court had also taken into consideration Exs.X2 and X3 i.e.,
Judgments dated 26.07.1984 in O.P No.146/1981 on the file of the II Additional Sub-Court, Kurnool and A.S No.2650 of 1987 dated 09.12.1988 of the High Court, respectively, wherein the market value of house sites fixed @ Rs.3,000/- per cent in respect of Gananpuram village, was settled before the Lok Adalat and subsequently, the appeal was dismissed, in view of the same.

8. The learned Reference Court after taking the said aspects into consideration, which were established by the respondent/claimant by adducing evidence, fixed the market value of the subject matter lands @ Rs.2,000/- per cent.

The said fixation in the light of ample evidence on record and for the cogent reasons assigned by the learned Reference Court, in the considered opinion of this The Special Deputy Collector vs N.Siva Reddy on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196969500/
2 Court, warrants no interference.
